subject: Archaeology
title: Neanderthals: Not the Brutes We Imagined
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Neanderthals: Not the Brutes We Imagined.

hook.text: Neanderthals buried their dead, made jewelry, and possibly painted caves. They were not stupid cavemen.

buildup.text: They lived across Europe and western Asia for over 300,000 years, surviving ice ages with sophisticated tools.

discovery.text: At Shanidar Cave in Iraq, a burial was found surrounded by pollen — suggesting the body was covered in flowers.

twist.text: DNA proves that most people outside Africa carry 1–4% Neanderthal genes. They did not just die out — they mixed with us.

climax.text: In 2018, cave paintings in Spain were dated to 65,000 years ago — made by Neanderthals, not modern humans.

punchline.text: They painted art, buried their dead, and live on in our DNA.

quiz.question: What did DNA analysis reveal about Neanderthals and modern humans?
options: Neanderthals and humans never interbred or interacted
Most people outside Africa carry 1–4% Neanderthal DNA
Neanderthals were a subspecies of Homo sapiens
